To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) BCANS is an online support group that is not a 'virtual community' in the sense of a place where people can'meet' and 'interact' in a'social' way.
BCANS is a vibrant online community that is both a source of emotional and social support and a forum for political action.

BCANS is a virtual community that provides a safe space where people can talk freely about breast cancer, where members can build social capital and trust, and where they can take action to improve the lives of breast cancer sufferers and their families.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of online medical communication and the ways in which people use cyberspace to support one another in the face of a life-threatening illness.
the social and political dimensions of medical communication in cyberspace, and with the potential of online communities for activism, advocacy, and social change.

the ways in which the BCANS online support group is a site for the creation, exchange and transformation of social capital, and with the implications of this phenomenon for the future of health communication and social policy. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2012 APA, all rights reserved)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BCANS community is a rich and complex example of how a virtual support group can provide a space for people to share their medical and personal experiences, to develop social capital, to create a community, and to become activists. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2010 APA, all rights reserved)
the Internet is a medium for medical communication that is both a powerful and a powerful tool, and a powerful tool for the study of the human world.

the Internet has created a new space for the exchange of information and support, and has enabled the formation of communities that would not exist otherwise, but that it is not clear that the Internet is a panacea for social ills, nor is it clear that the Internet will be the primary medium for future activism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the online community is not only a source of emotional support, but a source of practical information, a place for political action, and a source of empowerment.
the Internet has enabled a new form of social capital that has the potential to change the face of healthcare in Canada and beyond.
BCANS is a community of people who have been transformed into activists by their disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet is not just another medium for information exchange, but rather a social medium, a'social space' where individuals and groups can build relationships and social capital.
the Internet is a powerful and underutilized tool for improving the quality of life and health outcomes for people with serious diseases.
the Internet can serve as an empowering and enabling medium for medical communication, especially when it is used in conjunction with a nonprofit organization.
